cards.explanation: The answer is a shoot. Isaiah says, "Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse…" (Isaiah 11:1). Everybody figures a stump is finished, but something green comes up out of it anyway. I know a little about being written off, friends, and I like this kind of surprise.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "…a Branch from his roots will bear fruit." (Isaiah 11:1). Bearing fruit is the opposite of withering. A stump that was supposed to be done is about to produce, and I'm rooting for that stump.

The answer is delight. Isaiah says, "And He will delight in the fear of the LORD." (Isaiah 11:3). Delight means He's not dragging His feet about it. He enjoys it, and honestly, friends, I wish I enjoyed Monday mornings that much.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "He will not judge by what His eyes see, and He will not decide by what His ears hear…" (Isaiah 11:3). Not by what He sees, and not by what He hears. The text says what He will do instead in the next verse.

The answer is poor. Isaiah says, "…with righteousness He will judge the poor…" (Isaiah 11:4). The poor are the ones He judges with righteousness. The next line adds that He will decide with equity "…for the lowly of the earth."

The answer is the rod of His mouth. Isaiah says, "He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth…" (Isaiah 11:4). The rod is of His mouth, friends. I bet that's a picture of how much His words weigh.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist." (Isaiah 11:5). So He wears both righteousness and faithfulness. I can only dream of an outfit that good, and my apron has flour stains on it.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "The wolf will live with the lamb…" (Isaiah 11:6). A wolf and a lamb sharing a home is not the kind of roommate situation you see every day. Hunting isn't in the picture at all.

The answer is a little child. Isaiah says, "…and a little child will lead them." (Isaiah 11:6). The leader is a little child, in a verse full of leopards and young lions. I'd follow that child anywhere, friends, but I'd be hanging back a few steps.
The answer is True. Isaiah says, "…and the lion will eat straw like the ox." (Isaiah 11:7). A lion eating straw, friends. I don't think any lion has put that on a menu yet.
The answer is harming or destroying. Isaiah says, "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain…" (Isaiah 11:9). The verse says all My holy mountain, not just one slope of it.

The two words are knowledge and LORD. Isaiah says the earth "…will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water." (Isaiah 11:9). Knowledge fills the earth the way water fills the sea, so there's no dry spot. It's knowledge of the LORD that fills the earth, and the sea is the comparison for how full that knowledge will be.
The answer is nations. Isaiah says, "The nations will seek Him…" (Isaiah 11:10). The banner isn't just for one group, friends. It's for the peoples, and the nations come looking.

The answer is the four corners of the earth. Isaiah says, "He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth." (Isaiah 11:12). That's about as far apart as people can get. And He collects them anyway.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "Ephraim will no longer envy Judah, nor will Judah harass Ephraim." (Isaiah 11:13). The envy is gone, and the harassing is gone too. Peace between those two is quite a change.

The answer is True. Isaiah says the LORD "…will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals." (Isaiah 11:15). Crossing with dry sandals means nobody gets wet feet. I'm a big fan of dry feet, friends, especially around the bakery.

The answer is when Israel came up from Egypt. Isaiah says, "There will be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt." (Isaiah 11:16). It points back to that earlier journey out of Egypt. A highway will be there for them again.

The answer is that it has turned away. The speaker says, "Although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me." (Isaiah 12:1). The anger has turned away, and comfort has come. I can hear the relief in that line, friends.
The answer is True. The speaker says, "…Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me." (Isaiah 12:1). Comfort is named right there. I think the speaker is grateful for it, and I'd be too.

The answer is trust and not be afraid. The speaker says, "Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid." (Isaiah 12:2). Trusting and not being afraid goes together right after that line. I know a little about the dark, friends, and I like this one.
The answer is joy. Isaiah says, "With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation…" (Isaiah 12:3). They draw the water with joy. I'd say that's the best way to fill a bucket.
The answer is among the peoples. The words say, "Make His works known among the peoples…" (Isaiah 12:4). It's not kept inside one group, friends. It goes out to the peoples.

The answer is False. The words say, "Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things. Let this be known in all the earth." (Isaiah 12:5). That's the opposite of quiet. The glorious things are meant to be known everywhere.

The answer is False. The last line says, "Cry out and sing, O citizen of Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 12:6). The Holy One of Israel is great right among them. He's close, not far away.
